questiontext.text:
Assume the population of fish grows exponentially. A pond is stocked initially with \({@initial_no@} \,\,\textbf{fish}\). After \({@period_months@} \,\,\textbf{months}\), there are \({@dobled_no@}\,\, \textbf{fish}\) in the pond. The owner will allow his friends and neighbors to fish on his pond after the fish population reaches \({@dobled_no_results@}\). When will the owners friends be allowed to fish?


Give your answer correct to \(1dp\)

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]] \(\textbf{months}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

We know it takes the population of fish \({@period_months@}\) months to double in size. So, if \(𝑡\) represents time in months, by the doubling-time formula, we have \({@period_months@}={(\displaystyle\frac{\ln{2}}{k})}\). Then, \(𝑘={(\displaystyle\frac{\ln{2}}{{@period_months@}})}\)

Thus, the population is given by \(y={@initial_no@} \cdot e^{(\displaystyle\frac{\ln{2}}{{@period_months@}})t}\)

To figure out when the population reaches \({@dobled_no_results@}\) we solve the equation \(y={@initial_no@}\cdot e^{(\displaystyle\frac{\ln{2}}{{@period_months@}})t}\)

Where \(y\) is the final population of fish \(y={@dobled_no_results@}\)

\(y={@initial_no@}\cdot e^{(\displaystyle\frac{\ln{2}}{{@period_months@}})t}\)

\({@dobled_no_results@}=\displaystyle {@initial_no@}\cdot e^{\displaystyle (\frac{\ln{2}}{{@period_months@}})t}\)

\(\displaystyle{@(dobled_no_results/initial_no)@}=\displaystyle e^{\displaystyle (\frac{\ln{2}}{{@period_months@}})t}\)

\(\displaystyle{@log(dobled_no_results/initial_no)@}={@((log(2)/period_months)*t)@}\)

\(\displaystyle{@t=period_months*(log(dobled_no_results/initial_no)/log(2))@}\)

\(t={@decimalplaces(ta,2)@}\,\,\textbf{months}\)

Therefore, the period required to fish is \({@decimalplaces(ta,2)@}\)
